title: Attention kernel / paged-KV / continuous-batching — regression lab notes
summary: Lab-first writeup capturing a set of small but reproducible regressions observed after toggling the new flash-attention kernel and paged-KV eviction policy together with continuous batching enabled. This doc collects prompt-set level deltas, sample traces, e2e eval results, and short hypotheses for root cause plus actionable mitigations.
test_harness: Runner: ml-eval-v2 harness (container tag: eval-runner:2026-02-24). Models: fp16-open-7b-v1 (baseline kernels), fp16-open-7b-v1+flash (flash-attn enabled), fp16-open-7b-v1+flash+pagedkv (paged KV enabled), fp16-open-7b-v1+all (continuous-batching enabled). Hardware: p4d.24xlarge and local dev GPU (A10x4). Variants tested with sequence lengths: 128, 512, 1024, 2048; batching configs: microbatch=1/2/4, cont-batch-window=20ms/50ms/100ms. Measurements recorded: median latency (p50), p95 latency, tokens/sec, memory peak (GB), kv-evictions, kernel-fallback-counts. Logs collected with tracing: trace-id header applied, kv-metrics, kernel-selection debug enabled.
prompt_sets:
Three prompt sets used (short names):
1) mgmt-instr: 50 prompt templates (instruction format, ~40-120 tokens), heavy named-entity outputs.
2) dialogue-long: multi-turn chat prompts with historical context up to 1024 tokens; 200 examples.
3) codegen-snippets: code completion tasks with long sequences and nested brackets; 120 examples often pushing kv size.
Notes: each prompt set was run 10x per config; we captured raw outputs for quality-diff comparisons and tokenization-aligned logprobs for regression detection. Also included a small synthetic adversarial prompt list designed to stress KV eviction (kv-stress-12.txt).
eval_results:
High-level: most regressions are small but repeatable on certain combos.
- Baseline -> flash: no material quality regressions; latency improved ~10% median p50 for seq<=512.
- flash -> flash+pagedkv: observed tokens/sec drop at seq>=1024 and p95 latency spikes (2.5x) on p4d in ~12/200 dialogue-long cases.
- flash+pagedkv -> +continuous-batching: further variability: median latency sometimes improves for small batches but p95/p99 tail gets worse for dialogue-long when cont-batch-window >50ms.
Quantitative sample (dialogue-long, seq=1024, microbatch=2):
- baseline: p50=210ms, p95=420ms, tokens/sec=620
- flash: p50=180ms, p95=390ms, tokens/sec=700
- flash+pagedkv: p50=190ms, p95=1030ms, tokens/sec=350 (observed kv-eviction spikes)
- flash+pagedkv+contbatch(50ms): p50=170ms, p95=1200ms, tokens/sec=320 (occasionally CPU fallback observed)
Quality regressions (surface-level): 7/200 dialogue-long examples had formatting errors (missing closing tags) when paged-KV + cont-batch enabled; likely due to partial KV misses during streaming decode. Exact logprobs showed abrupt drop in token probability around eviction boundaries.
regression_examples:
Example A (dialogue-long #87):
- Prompt: user asked multi-turn question referencing earlier session
- Baseline output: coherent multi-sentence answer with correct reference
- flash+pagedkv output: answer truncated mid-sentence at the turn boundary; final tokens: '<assistant> I think the best approach is' and then termination.
Trace excerpt: kernel-selection=flash, kv-load-time=14ms, kv-evict-count=3 during decode; at token-234 we saw kvcache-miss-on-read and a synchronous block causing request to fall back to CPU kernel for 80ms.
Example B (codegen-snippets #42):
- Baseline: completed function with closing brace
- flash+pagedkv+contbatch(100ms): missing closing brace and indentation broken. Logprobs show mismatch where context window used older KV page leading to shifted generation.
Repro command (internal): ./run_eval --config tests/attn_pagedkv_contbatch.yaml --example 87 --trace
Attached raw traces in linked_artifacts (confluence page).
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Eviction timing + continuous-batching window interacts such that in-flight requests see inconsistent KV pages (read-old, then eviction, then read-miss) leading to semantic context loss.
2) Flash-attention kernel has an edge-case where certain seqLen & microbatch combinations trigger an unaligned memory access on A10y that forces a synchronous copy, increasing p95 and causing kernel-fallbacks.
3) Race in kernel-selection path: cont-batch aggregator may merge requests with different KV lifetimes, and paged-KV eviction didn't mark the merged trace correctly.
Evidence:
- Kernel-fallback-count correlates strongly with p95 spikes in traces where kv-evict-count>0.
- CPU fallback traces show a short period (~40-120ms) of blocked decode before resuming; these blocks align with eviction events in kv logs.
- Reproduced locally on A10x4 with synthetic kv-stress: toggling eviction-threshold from 64MB->128MB reduces occurrences by ~60%.
Open questions:
- Do different backends (p4d vs a10x4) surface different failure modes due to SDK cuda driver versions?
- Is there a correctable ordering guarantee missing between cont-batch flush and paged-KV eviction callback?
action_items:
1) Add stronger invariants in cont-batch merge: ensure combined requests have matched KV lifetimes or reject merge — assigned to Marco Liu — ENG-5583.
2) Instrument paged-KV with a global generation id and assert reads include gen check; add unit test around eviction-read races — assigned to Ben Cole — PR #8721.
3) Add a temporary guard: if kv-evict-count>0 during decode, prefer synchronous pipeline (slightly higher median latency but avoids tail spikes) — short-term patch, owner Sofia Ramirez.
4) Expand eval harness to include kv-stress-12 in CI and run full dialogue-long set nightly for a week after patch — owner Aisha Patel.
5) Add kernel-selection debug telemetry to correlate kernel fallback with driver version and microbatch sizes — owner Marco Liu.
Estimated impact: items 1-3 should reduce p95 regressions by ~70%.
next_steps:
Short term (48-72h):
- Branch and PR for paged-KV generation id + test (Ben).
- Quick cont-batch merge protection rollback option toggled via feature flag for canary (Marco).
- Nightly run configured with new metrics; alert on p95 regressions >30% (Aisha).
Medium term (2-4 weeks):
- Perf regression sweep across seqLen grid with new invariant enforced; measure cost impact of fallback guard.
- Postmortem-style doc if we hit customer-facing incidents; contact CS for any customers on Dedicated with heavy long-context workloads.
Notes to reviewers: this doc mixes experimental log excerpts and hypotheses; please annotate with references to PRs or counter-evidence if you reproduced different behavior. If you can't reproduce locally, record exact driver/CUDA/cudnn/runtime versions — we suspect driver differences matter.
body:
Raw lab journal (chronological):

2025-11-18 09:12 — kicked off first run using eval-runner:2025-11-17. Noticed improvement p50 at seq<=512 across matrix, all good.
2025-11-18 12:45 — enabling paged-KV introduced occasional p95 spike on dialogue-long; looked like eviction spikes.
2025-11-19 08:02 — reproduced locally on A10x4 using kv-stress-12; traced a read-miss then eviction then sync fallback.
2025-11-20 14:10 — toggled eviction threshold to 128MB; p95 spikes reduced but still present on some examples.
2025-12-02 11:00 — enabled continuous-batching in combination; microbatch merge occasionally combined requests with unequal KV life leading to mismatched context. Repro rate ~6% on dialogue-long, seq>=1024.
2025-12-05 16:30 — ran with kernel debug enabled: found kernel-selection fallback occurs right after an eviction callback. Suspect ordering issue between cont-batch flush and eviction callback.
2026-01-09 09:00 — ran longer sweep on p4d; behavior similar but frequency lower; p4d driver stack appears to hide some synchronous copies but not all.
Feedback loop: recorded traces and pushed small reproducer (kv-repro/evict-repro.py) to github PR #8721.

Unresolved notes / TODOs:
- Add a minimal unit test that simulates two requests with adjacent KV pages and forces eviction mid-decode.
- Confirm whether streaming-decoder path (incremental token emission) interacts differently than batch decode path.
- Validate that changing cont-batch-window to <=10ms eliminates most merges; measure throughput cost.

If you run these reproductions, please paste command and exact docker tag and cuda version into the PR review comments.

End of lab notes.
